notes: PM2.5: near the four monitored cities (within 30 km) a per-city correction of the CAMS global forecast; in cities, towns and suburbs elsewhere the national PM2.5 model (CAMS composition, the day's weather and the 250 m surface, trained on 354 low-cost sensors; with each monitored city held out it cut the daily error at the monitors from 43 to 26 ug/m3). In rural and high-mountain places (no sensors there) and where a composition input is missing the raw CAMS value is shown, marked. Days 2-5 carry the composition forecast's own error.
Crop burning upwind: NASA FIRMS satellite fire detections of the last 3 days within 300 km, weighted toward the forecast wind direction; it explains a smog day, it does not change it.
Dispersion uses the ventilation index (boundary-layer height × wind) and morning inversions; it flags smog-trapping weather regardless of emissions.
Not yet verified against PM2.5 monitors.

temperature: Daily maximum temperature: off by 1.47 °C on average on forecast day 1 (1.5–1.6 °C over days 1 to 3) and about 0.3–0.4 °C too cool; daily minimum: off by 1.53 °C on day 1 and about 1.1–1.2 °C too warm; for the minimum the corrected forecast is slightly worse than the uncorrected model (1.48 °C on day 1) (stations never used in training, 1 Jan–30 Sep 2026)
Hourly temperature, measured after the model’s fitting window (27 Sep–11 Oct 2026): plains off by 1.30 °C, mountains 1.98 °C (about 1.0 °C too cold), hills 2.57 °C (about 2.1 °C too cold)
The 90 % range held 94–95 % of hours overall, 85 % in the hills and 97.5 % in the mountains (where it is about 10 °C wide); plains daily maxima and minima fell inside it 86–89 % of the time
heat: Heat stress at Moderate or higher, forecast days 1 and 2, Sindh and Punjab (2–18 Oct 2026, checked at 24 standard weather and airport stations over 16 days): the level caught 93 % of the observed Moderate-or-higher days (95 % interval 88–97 %), and 10 % of its Moderate-or-higher forecasts were false alarms (5–16 %); it did better than carrying the last observed level forward. Elsewhere in Pakistan, and on the day of issue and day 3, the heat level is not yet verified

Heat stress at High or Severe (same check): 53 % of these forecasts were false alarms (95 % interval 38–66 %) and the level did not beat carrying the last observed level forward, so High and Severe are indicative and raise no alerts
cold: Cold stress: no event test yet: no cold-stress day was observed and none forecast in the 1,119 station-days of the test window (26 Sep–14 Oct 2026), so the level could not be tested; it is indicative and raises no alerts
